changeSet.author: echno
changeSet.comment:
The marks drawn over defect photographs, for the annotated defect images the QA/QC report prints.
Keyed by inspection_id and by the photo reference itself, not by defect_id. An inspection's defects are rebuilt wholesale on every save (see the ncrs changelog), so every defect row is deleted and reinserted under a new id each time an inspector saves; a child of the defect row would be destroyed with it. The photo reference survives that rebuild unchanged, and it is what the mark actually describes.
There is no foreign key on photo either: inspection_defect_photos is an element collection with no row identity to point at. The consequence is deliberate. When a photograph is replaced it arrives under a new key, the old marks match nothing, and DefectAnnotationService deletes them. Carrying a mark onto a replacement image would be worse than losing it: the coordinates describe a region of specific pixels, so the mark would keep claiming to be evidence while pointing somewhere meaningless.
The four coordinates are fractions of the image width and height rather than pixels, so a mark holds its place whether it is drawn on a thumbnail in the web app or a half-page plate in the PDF, and nothing stored depends on the resolution of the file or the device that took it. The CHECK constraint enforces the range in the schema, because a coordinate off the image cannot be drawn and cannot be read.

changeSet.author: echno
changeSet.comment: Coordinates are fractions of the image, so every one of them is between zero and one. Enforced here as well as in the request validation: the validation stops a bad payload, this stops a bad row whatever wrote it.
changeSet.sql: ALTER TABLE inspection_defect_annotations ADD CONSTRAINT ck_defect_annotation_bounds CHECK (x1 BETWEEN 0 AND 1 AND y1 BETWEEN 0 AND 1 AND x2 BETWEEN 0 AND 1 AND y2 BETWEEN 0 AND 1)

rollback.sql: ALTER TABLE inspection_defect_annotations DROP CONSTRAINT ck_defect_annotation_bounds
